newsitem.title: ITALY: BankItaly rate cuts will balance fiscal policy - DB.
newsitem.headline: BankItaly rate cuts will balance fiscal policy - DB.

text.p: The Bank of Italy's monetary policy, with the goal of inflation under 3.0 percent by end-1996 now achieved, should in 1997 be more geared towards counterbalancing the effects of the government's restrictive fiscal policy, Deutsche Bank Milan said in a market note.
"The more signs there will be of an economic slowdown, the more the Bank of Italy's attitude will be accommodating," the bank said.

"Even assuming a discount rate cut of 200 basis points by next summer (including last week's 75 bps cut to 7.50 percent), we forecast real GDP growth of 1.1 percent in 1997, well under the government's 2.0 percent target. Such a level would require a rate cut of at least 350 bps," it said.
Deutsche Bank said parliamentary approval of the 1997 budget and a non-inflationary agreement on contracts for engineers and metalworkers would determine the timescale for the next cut.
A solution of these two factors "should open the way for a further rate reduction which we do not exclude being before the end of the year and of the order of 50 basis points," the note added.
